hooks.text: Our universe could vanish in an instant with zero warning.
A bubble of true vacuum could expand at light speed.
Standard Model calculations estimate vacuum lifetimes exceeding 10 to the 65 years.

title: The Bubble That Could Erase Our Universe
description: Explore false vacuum decay, a hypothetical cosmic catastrophe where a true vacuum bubble could instantly rewrite physics.

beats.text: Our universe could vanish in an instant with zero warning.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of cosmic expansion and space, 2020

beats.text: This terrifying possibility stems from false vacuum decay, a metastable state where local stability could suddenly collapse.
beats.visual: Illustration of quantum field vacuum energy landscape, 2021

beats.text: The theoretical framework for this catastrophic process was established by Sidney Coleman in 1977.
beats.visual: Photograph of Harvard physics department exterior, 1977

beats.text: Standard Model calculations place the electroweak vacuum in this fragile, metastable region.
beats.visual: CERN Large Hadron Collider CMS detector tunnel, 2012

beats.text: Calculations of the Standard Model vacuum lifetime estimate it exceeds 10 to the 65 to 10 to the 100 years.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope deep space view, 2014

beats.text: Yet researchers recently simulated these universe-destroying bubbles using a 5,564-qubit quantum annealer from D-Wave.
Published in Nature Physics in 2025, these findings prove a bubble of true vacuum could expand at the speed of light.
beats.visual: Illustration of an expanding true vacuum bubble, 2025

beats.text: Because a bubble of true vacuum could expand at light speed, our universe could vanish in an instant with zero warning.
beats.visual: Physicist working in a quantum physics laboratory, 2025
